financials_interim.notes: HNB is a licensed commercial bank; following this project's bank/NBFI mapping convention: revenue = Total Operating Income (net interest income + net fee/commission income + net trading/FVOCI gains + insurance premium income (Group only) + other operating income), the bank's own P&L subtotal. operating_profit = 'Operating profit before taxes on financial services' (before VAT-on-Financial-Services/SSCL). PBT reconciles as operating_profit_after_taxes_on_financial_services + share of profit of equity-accounted investees (Group only, Rs 82,060k in 2026 vs Rs 395,666k in 2025) = printed PBT (ties exactly for Bank; ties to within Rs1'000 rounding for Group: 37,194,404+82,060=37,276,464 vs printed 37,276,465). finance_costs/finance_income intentionally left blank: the bank's operating_profit subtotal already nets interest income against interest expense inside Total Operating Income, so populating separate finance_cost/finance_income fields would double-count against operating_profit and break the operating_profit+finance_income-finance_costs=PBT identity check used elsewhere in this project. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank -- banks use a liquidity-ordered balance sheet with no current/non-current split and the loan book is not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = Due to banks + Securities sold under repurchase agreements; long_term_borrowings = Other borrowings at amortised cost + Debt securities issued + Subordinated term debts -- both judgment calls given the filing gives no maturity breakdown of these lines, documented here for transparency. Due to depositors (customer deposits) is explicitly EXCLUDED from both borrowing fields per project convention. Verification: balance sheet identity ties exactly for both Bank and Group; PBT-tax=PAT ties to within Rs1'000 rounding for both. No dual-rendering column-swap artifact found -- Bank and Group columns are clearly separately labelled throughout and every figure ties to its own printed %-change column. (Bank/standalone basis: no NCI, no share of associate profit.)

interim_updates.note_text: HNB Group's Total Operating Income rose 24.3% YoY to Rs 101.83bn for H1 FY2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026), driven by a 23.1% increase in net interest income to Rs 66.74bn (NIM up to 4.40% from 4.26%) and a 26.8% increase in net fee and commission income to Rs 14.04bn (digital banking, card transactions, transaction banking and leasing). By segment, Corporate banking grew fastest: Corporate net interest income rose from Rs 6.46bn to Rs 11.09bn (+71.6%) and Corporate segment operating income rose from Rs 9.52bn to Rs 15.61bn (+64.0%), while Retail NII grew a more modest 17.4% (Rs 14.69bn to Rs 17.24bn) and Treasury segment operating income fell 7.2% (Rs 18.95bn to Rs 17.58bn) as Treasury NII slipped 3.6%. The NBFI segment (HNB Finance PLC) grew operating income 39.4% (Rs 4.77bn to Rs 6.65bn). Despite this strong top-line growth, Group PAT fell 2.6% YoY to Rs 22.56bn because impairment charges swung from a Rs 4.84bn net reversal in H1 FY2025 to a Rs 5.03bn net charge in H1 FY2026 -- a negative swing of Rs 9.87bn -- driven mainly by the Corporate segment, where impairment moved from a Rs 4.65bn reversal to a Rs 2.79bn charge (a ~Rs 7.44bn swing), and the SME segment, where it moved from an Rs 86mn reversal to a Rs 1.04bn charge (~Rs 1.13bn swing). The Investment Banking segment also swung from a Rs 2.76bn operating income contribution in H1 FY2025 to a Rs 295mn operating loss in H1 FY2026. Operating expenses were well controlled (cost-to-income improved to 34.48% from 37.82%), and share of associate profit fell 79.3% (Rs 395,666k to Rs 82,060k) -- a minor drag. Bank (standalone) PAT of Rs 23.14bn actually rose 9.2% YoY, diverging from the Group figure because the Group number consolidates HNB Finance PLC, HNB Life PLC, Sithma Development and HNB Investment Bank, and it is the Group-level impairment and Investment Banking swings above that pull the consolidated figure down relative to the Bank standalone result.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for HNB -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. YoY comparison uses the filing's own prior-year comparative column (six months ended 30 June 2025). The filing's own balance-sheet comparative is versus 31 Dec 2025 (FYE, audited), not 30 June 2025, consistent with standard interim SOFP presentation -- this is NOT used for any QoQ purpose, only as the filing's own point-in-time comparative.
interim_updates.takeaway: Core banking income and margins strengthened materially (NII +23%, fees +27%, NIM up to 4.40%), but reported Group PAT still fell 2.6% YoY purely because of a Rs 9.87bn negative swing in impairment charges (mostly Corporate and SME segments) against a large reversal booked in the prior-year comparative -- the underlying franchise is growing faster than the headline Group PAT number suggests, and Bank-standalone PAT (+9.2% YoY) confirms this.

operational_highlights: Group Total Operating Income +24.3% YoY to Rs 101.83bn (Bank +27.2% to Rs 76.74bn)
Net Interest Margin improved to 4.40% from 4.26%; Group Net Interest Income +23.1% YoY to Rs 66.74bn
Group net fee and commission income +26.8% YoY to Rs 14.04bn, led by digital banking, cards, transaction banking and leasing
Gross loans and advances (Group) grew Rs 224bn (+14.8%) in H1 FY2026 to Rs 1.82Tn; customer deposits grew Rs 138bn to surpass Rs 2.1Tn
Net Stage 3 (NPL) ratio held at 1.17% (vs 1.09% at FYE2025); Tier 1 Capital Ratio 15.44%, Total Capital Ratio 18.18%, all-currency LCR 186.69%
key_drivers: Impairment charges swung Rs 9.87bn negatively YoY (Rs 5.03bn net charge vs Rs 4.84bn net reversal in H1 FY2025), driven primarily by the Corporate segment (~Rs 7.44bn swing) and SME segment (~Rs 1.13bn swing), reflecting the significant expansion of the lending book
Investment Banking segment swung from a Rs 2.76bn operating income contribution to a Rs 295mn operating loss YoY
NBFI segment (HNB Finance PLC) operating income +39.4% YoY to Rs 6.65bn
Treasury segment operating income -7.2% YoY (Rs 18.95bn to Rs 17.58bn) as Treasury NII fell 3.6%, partially offsetting strong Corporate/Retail/SME growth
